skill.name: chakra-ui-refactor
skill.description: Review, convert, and improve UI code using Chakra UI v3. Use this skill whenever a user wants to review Chakra UI code for issues, convert plain HTML/CSS, Tailwind, CSS Modules, or styled-components to Chakra UI, clean up messy Chakra components, fix layout structure or token usage, or asks anything like "is this correct", "what's wrong with this", "review my component", "refactor this", "clean up", "convert", or "chakra-ify this" — even without the words "review" or "refactor". Trigger on any request to check, improve, or convert Chakra UI code, however casually phrased.
skill.summary: Review and refactor Chakra UI v3 components for accessibility, responsive layouts, correct APIs, and consistent design tokens.
skill.author: chakra-ui

security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, UI terminology, and illustrative component code. No evidence found of malicious execution, reconnaissance, data exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. The skill provides UI review and conversion instructions, including conditional removal of unused styling dependencies.

buttons, `htmlFor`/`id` on label+input pairs, `alt` on images)
- Does the heading hierarchy make sense? (no skipped levels, no `h1` used as a
- Are form fields wrapped in `Field.Root` with `Field.Label` and
- Would this break on mobile? (fixed widths, `overflow: hidden` on small
- Are v3 prop names used? (`disabled` not `isDisabled`, `colorPalette` not
- Is `"use client"` placed correctly in Next.js App Router?
- Are there v2 patterns still present? (`extendTheme`, `ColorModeScript`,
- Are hardcoded colors used where semantic tokens would work? (`bg="#f9fafb"` →
- Are there inline `style={{}}` props that should be Chakra style props?
- Is there unnecessary nesting? (`Box > Box > Box` when one would do)
- Is manual spacing (`mt={4}` on every child) used where `Stack gap={4}` would
- Are the right layout primitives used? (`Flex` vs `Stack` vs `Grid` vs
- Interactive `Box` with `onClick` but no keyboard access
- Wrong v3 prop name that silently does nothing (`isDisabled` doesn't disable in
- `"use client"` missing on a component that uses hooks in App Router
**From CSS Modules** — convert what you can to Chakra props; keep `className`
- Flatten `Box > Box > Box` nesting; replace `mt`/`mb` on every child with
- Replace `sx` with `css` (v3 rename); update nested `&:hover` selectors inside
- Replace `bg="gray.50"` → `bg="bg.subtle"` and other semantic token equivalents
- Keep `aria-*` attributes; add missing ones where clearly needed
- Keep semantic HTML intent (`<nav>` → `Box as="nav"`, not just `Box`)
- Keep `"use client"` where it exists; add it only when the component genuinely
- Don't add `"use client"` just because a component uses Chakra UI

content.user_title: Review and Refactor Chakra UI v3 Components
content.value_statement: UI components can contain outdated APIs, inaccessible controls, and inconsistent layouts. This skill guides focused reviews and Chakra UI v3 conversions while preserving existing behavior.
actual_capabilities: Structure component reviews by behavioral impact, with targeted fixes for significant issues.
Check accessible labels, keyboard interaction, heading hierarchy, and form field associations.
Convert HTML/CSS, Tailwind, CSS Modules, and styled-components patterns into Chakra UI props and components.
Identify outdated Chakra properties and suggest v3 names and compound component structures.
Simplify nested layouts and replace hardcoded styles with responsive props and semantic tokens.
Preserve event handlers, state, semantic markup, and necessary Next.js client boundaries during refactoring.
limitations: Requires actual component code and enough project context; it does not review descriptions alone.
Provides instructions rather than a bundled migration script or automated test suite.
Some complex selectors and animations may still require CSS classes.
Generated changes require project validation; examples and token mappings may need adjustment for your installed version and theme.

use_cases.title: Review a React component before merging
use_cases.description: Identify accessibility, API, and responsive layout issues, with targeted corrections instead of a full rewrite.

use_cases.title: Convert a styled prototype
use_cases.description: Translate Tailwind or HTML/CSS components into Chakra UI while retaining interaction logic and semantic structure.

use_cases.title: Standardize shared component patterns
use_cases.description: Review repeated styles, outdated properties, and token inconsistencies, then suggest reusable components or recipes.

prompt_templates.title: Review one component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the component below as Chakra UI v3. Identify accessibility and API issues, show minimal fixes, and do not rewrite the whole component.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: paste a component for a focused critique.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Tailwind component
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the Tailwind component below to Chakra UI v3. Preserve handlers, state, semantic HTML, and responsive behavior. Explain the main changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: migrate an existing component between styling systems.

prompt_templates.title: Clean up a Chakra layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the Chakra component below. Reduce unnecessary nesting, replace suitable hardcoded colors with semantic tokens, and preserve existing behavior. State your assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve layout structure and styling consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Review and migrate a Next.js component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review and refactor the Next.js component below for Chakra UI v3. Check compound APIs, accessibility, responsive props, and client boundaries. Preserve framework components and interactions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: include the installed version, theme context, and framework details with the component.

output_examples.input: Review a dialog close button that has an icon but no accessible label.
output: Critical: the close button has no accessible name.
Targeted fix: add an accessible label describing the close action.
Keep the existing close handler and dialog state unchanged.

output_examples.input: Convert a Tailwind profile panel with responsive spacing and a save action to Chakra UI v3.
output: Refactored structure: use Chakra layout primitives and spacing props.
Responsive changes: translate breakpoint classes into responsive prop values.
Behavior preserved: retain the save handler, state, and conditional content.

output_examples.input: Clean up a Chakra component with nested wrappers and hardcoded background colors.
output: Simplify redundant wrappers while preserving semantic elements.
Replace repeated child margins with shared layout spacing.
Use suitable semantic background tokens and explain the styling changes.

best_practices: Provide the component, installed Chakra version, framework, and relevant theme context.
Specify whether you need a review, a refactor, or both.
Validate types, keyboard interactions, responsive layouts, and visual behavior after applying changes.
anti_patterns: Requesting a review without sharing the actual component code.
Replacing every style mechanically when complex CSS or custom theme behavior requires exceptions.
Removing styling dependencies without checking whether other components still use them.

faq.question: Which Chakra UI version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Chakra UI v3 by default and asks the assistant to check the installed version first.

faq.question: Can I request a review without a full rewrite?
faq.answer: Yes. Review mode provides categorized findings and minimal fixes rather than replacing the complete component.

faq.question: Which styling approaches can it help convert?
faq.answer: It covers HTML/CSS, Tailwind, CSS Modules, styled-components, and existing Chakra UI components.

faq.question: Does it guarantee accessible components?
faq.answer: No. It guides accessibility review, but keyboard testing and other project checks remain necessary.

faq.question: Can it help with Next.js components?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses client boundaries and composing Chakra wrappers with Next.js Link and Image.

faq.question: Does the skill include an automated migration tool?
faq.answer: No. It contains instructions for an AI assistant, not a bundled executable, migration script, or test runner.
